tools.name: build_dna.py
tools.usage: build_dna.py [-h] [--cg-input] -o PREFIX [--sirah-dir SIRAH_DIR] [--salt M] [--cation {NaW,KW}] [--no-ztype] [--g4-cation {KW4,NW4}] [--g4-site {between,plane}] [--g4-tips] [--no-g4-cations] [--ring-bond RES.ATOM:RES.ATOM] [--no-end-restraint] [--no-decks] [--tleap-bin TLEAP_BIN] input_pdb
tools.doc:
Build an AMBER-ready ηθDNA 1.0 CG system from an all-atom, DNA-only PDB.

    python build_dna.py input.pdb -o outdir/name --sirah-dir /path/to/sirah

Pipeline: all-atom PDB -> CG PDB (cg_dna.convert_dna: repeated-base
retyping, 5'/3' caps) -> G-quadruplex channel cations if the structure has
tetrads (cg_dna.g4) -> tleap (SIRAH WT4 water, neutralization, NaCl 0.15 M
by default) -> the v18 topology chain (cg_dna.cmap, cg_dna.topology) ->
WC end restraint (DISANG) + AMBER decks + run_md.sh.

One system per output directory: outdir/ receives name.prmtop,
name.inpcrd, the decks (em/eq/md/md2_WT4.in, plus dens_WT4.in at high
salt), disang.rst, run_md.sh and build_summary.json; intermediates go to
outdir/build/. Then:  bash outdir/run_md.sh name

Requirements: tleap on PATH (AmberTools), the parmed and numpy Python
packages, and a local SIRAH installation (http://www.sirahff.com; not
bundled, point --sirah-dir or $SIRAH_HOME at it).

options.help: all-atom PDB, DNA only (protein chains are skipped -- see build_dna_protein.py)
input_pdb is already a CG PDB (ηθDNA bead names, e.g. from convert_dna.py)

tools.name: build_dna_protein.py
tools.usage: build_dna_protein.py [-h] [--cg-input] [--ph PH] [--pdb2pqr-bin PDB2PQR_BIN] -o PREFIX [--sirah-dir SIRAH_DIR] [--salt M] [--cation {NaW,KW}] [--no-ztype] [--g4-cation {KW4,NW4}] [--g4-site {between,plane}] [--g4-tips] [--no-g4-cations] [--ring-bond RES.ATOM:RES.ATOM] [--no-end-restraint] [--no-decks] [--tleap-bin TLEAP_BIN] input_pdb
tools.doc:
Build an AMBER-ready ηθDNA 1.0 + SIRAH-protein CG system from one
all-atom PDB of a DNA-protein complex.

    python build_dna_protein.py input.pdb -o outdir/name --sirah-dir /path/to/sirah

Pipeline: split the input into DNA and protein -> DNA via cg_dna.convert_dna
(this model's mapping) -> protein via pdb2pqr (protonation) + SIRAH's
cgconv.pl -> merged CG PDB -> tleap (`source leaprc.sirah` + this model's
DNA parameters on top; neutralize with NaW and ClW, NaCl 0.15 M by
default) -> the ηθDNA 1.0 topology chain (DNA residues only; SIRAH's protein
force field is untouched) -> WC end restraint on the DNA + the SIRAH
multi-stage decks (em1, em2, eq1, eq2, md, md2) + run_md.sh.

Requirements beyond build_dna.py's: `pdb2pqr` on PATH (pip install pdb2pqr)
and `perl` on PATH (to run SIRAH's bundled cgconv.pl).

options.help: all-atom PDB containing both DNA and protein chains
input_pdb is already a combined CG PDB (SIRAH protein + ηθDNA beads)
pH for the PROPKA protonation states (default 7.0)
pdb2pqr executable (default: pdb2pqr)

tools.name: backmap_dna.py
tools.usage: backmap_dna.py [-h] [--traj NC [NC ...]] -o PREFIX [--n-frames N_FRAMES] [--jobs JOBS] [--resolvate] [--keep-scratch] [--allow-unmapped] [--no-conformers] [--maxcyc MAXCYC] [--ncyc NCYC] [--cutoff CUTOFF] [--tleap-bin TLEAP_BIN] [--sander-bin SANDER_BIN] [--cpptraj-bin CPPTRAJ_BIN] cg_prmtop [traj_dir]
tools.doc:
Recover an all-atom trajectory from a finished ηθDNA CG MD run (model
1.0 or the v17 development model; DNA-only or DNA+protein/SIRAH) -- the
reverse of build_dna.py / build_dna_protein.py.

    python backmap_dna.py cg.prmtop traj_dir -o out/system --n-frames 50
    python backmap_dna.py cg.prmtop --traj md.nc md2.nc -o out/x --n-frames 20

Pipeline, per selected frame: extract the CG frame (cpptraj) ->
geometrically reconstruct heavy atoms (NeRF, cg_backmap.reconstruct) ->
add hydrogens + a short vacuum minimization (tleap + sander, same protocol
SIRAH's own backmapping tool uses). Frames are then combined into one
multi-frame AMBER NetCDF trajectory + shared prmtop.

Each nucleotide's sugar and backbone come from the conformer template
(B, A, syn or Z; params/backmap_dna.json) that best fits its CG beads,
picked per nucleotide and per frame; --no-conformers builds them all
with the B template.

Water and bulk-ion CG beads are dropped (never geometrically backmapped,
matching SIRAH's own documented behavior). G4 channel cations (KW4/NW4)
are kept, as K+/Na+ at the bead position. The output is solute plus
channel cations by default; pass --resolvate to re-solvate the
(topologically identical) frame-0 structure with real explicit water
afterward.

No SIRAH installation needed at runtime (unlike the forward pipeline):
SIRAH's own protein/water NeRF recipe was extracted once and is bundled
in this repo -- only AmberTools (tleap/sander/cpptraj) + parmed + numpy
are required.

Known limitation: protein protonation state (HID/HIE/HIP/etc., set by the
forward pipeline's pdb2pqr step) is not recoverable from SIRAH's CG
protein beads -- SIRAH's own CG mapping is protonation-state-agnostic.
tleap assigns its own default protonation state during hydrogenation.

options.help: the finished CG run's prmtop
directory containing md.nc, md2.nc, ... chunks (mutually exclusive with --traj)
explicit trajectory chunk file(s), in order, instead of traj_dir
output path prefix, e.g. out/1bna_backmap
number of evenly-spaced frames to backmap (default: 50)
parallel frames (each runs its own tleap+sander); default: 1 (serial)
also re-solvate frame 0's structure with explicit water
keep the per-frame scratch directory instead of deleting it
drop (with a warning) any CG residue type with no backmap recipe, instead of failing
build every nucleotide with the B template (1BNA) instead of picking B/A/syn/Z per nucleotide
sander minimization: total steps (default: 150, matches SIRAH's own default)
sander minimization: steepest-descent steps before switching to conjugate-gradient (default: 100)
sander minimization: electrostatic cutoff in Angstrom (default: 12.0)
tleap executable (default: tleap)
sander executable (default: sander)
cpptraj executable (default: cpptraj)

common.help: output prefix, e.g. out/1bna/1bna (one system per directory)
path to a local SIRAH install (or set $SIRAH_HOME)
salt concentration on top of neutralization, SIRAH rule (default 0.15; 0 = neutralize only; the Z-DNA benchmark used 3.0)
bulk cation for neutralization and salt: NaW (NaCl, default) or KW (KCl)
do not apply the Z typing (Z-DNA G/C detected in the input keep the B parameters)
G4 channel cation placed when the input has none in the channel (default KW4 = K+)
G4 cation sites: between tetrads (K+, default) or in the tetrad planes (Na+, use with NW4)
also place a cation outside each outer tetrad
stop instead of placing channel cations when tetrads are found
extra bond for tleap, e.g. 182.C4G:1.PA to close a circular strand (repeat per strand)
no WC distance restraint on the terminal pairs
only the topology and coordinates, no decks or run_md.sh

run_md:
ηθDNA 1.0: runs one replica of a system built by build_dna.py / build_dna_protein.py, up to TARGET_NS of production.
Resume-safe: re-launch it and it continues from the last finished stage.

  bash run_md.sh <name> [TARGET_NS=1000]       (run from anywhere; works in the directory of this script)

DNA (decks em/eq/md/md2): EM on CPU with the solute restrained -> [compaction if dens_WT4.in exists, high salt;
  a warning in run_md.log if the volume has not settled after 40 x 50 ps]
  -> EQ 750 ps NPT with a 0->100->298 K ramp -> production in 100 ns chunks (md, md2, md3, ...).
DNA-protein (decks em1/em2/eq1/eq2/md/md2): em1 (backbone restrained) and em2 (whole solute) on CPU
  -> eq1 5 ns (ramp to 300 K, solute restrained) -> eq2 25 ns (backbone, wt 0.24) -> production in 100 ns chunks.
The EM runs on CPU (pmemd; sander if pmemd fails): on pmemd.cuda an ion placed next to a base can overflow the
energy accumulator (-8.59e9) and leave the minimizer in a false minimum.

Environment: AMBER on PATH (or AMBERHOME, or /opt/amber24, /opt/amber22).
  WAIT_GPU=1 (default) waits until no other compute process uses the GPU before each GPU stage, so two runs never
  share it. Set WAIT_GPU=0 on a cluster that assigns GPUs for you.

water, ions, ...) is silently dropped -- see convert_protein.py for the
DNA+protein pipeline.
